Useful when something does not work
127.0.0.1 — this device only. 0.0.0.0 — reachable by the whole local network.
Any free port from 1 to 65535. Use the same value in Telegram.
The password Telegram authenticates with. Keep it private; regenerating it means re-adding the proxy.
Default: 2:149.154.167.220, 4:149.154.167.220. Clear the field if photos and videos do not load.

The domain name never leaves in one piece: the TLS handshake is cut into two TLS records in the middle of the name, and an HTTP request (port 80) in the middle of the Host header. Defeats filters that only parse the first packet or the first TLS record — the usual case with ISPs and mobile operators. Costs nothing; leave it on.
0 — send both parts immediately. 10–50 ms helps against filters that reassemble packets, but adds that delay to every new connection.

Normally the app tries Telegram\'s own domain first and only substitutes a neutral one after a timeout. Enable this to substitute right away — saves 5–7 seconds per connection on a network that blocks Telegram by name.
The name shown to the network instead of Telegram\'s. Must be a site your operator does not block.
Keep out of the VPN tunnel

While a VPN is up, the proxy keeps its own connections on the normal network, so Telegram traffic does not go through the VPN. Other apps are unaffected. If the VPN forbids connections outside the tunnel, the app falls back to using it and writes that to the log.
When the phone is on mobile data, force the TLS split and the neutral domain for the session even if they are off above. Applies when the proxy starts.
Probing Telegram servers — can take up to half a minute…
Wraps the connection between Telegram and this app in something that looks like TLS to the given site. Applies to the local link only.
If a direct WebSocket fails, connect through public Cloudflare-proxied domains. Slower, but usually works.
Your own domains behind Cloudflare instead of the public ones. Needs setup on the Cloudflare side.

A route through your own Cloudflare Worker (docs/CfWorker.md in the desktop project). Races with the other routes; a domain without a scheme is tried over both TLS and plain HTTP and the working one is remembered. A self-hosted relay can go in “Whitelist bypass”.
Connections opened in advance so Telegram connects instantly. More means faster start and slightly more battery. 0 disables it.
Larger values speed up big downloads and use more RAM. 256 KB suits most cases.
For developers only. Regular accounts do not work on the test network.
Starts the proxy right after a reboot, without opening the app.
Writes details about every connection to the log. Turn on while diagnosing, off afterwards.
Keeps the MTProto proxy running in the background
Minimal notification without counters or buttons

Removes counters and the Stop button, hides the notification from the lock screen and collapses it at the bottom of the shade. Android does not allow removing it completely — a background service without a notification gets killed by the system. To hide it entirely, turn the notification off in system settings; the proxy keeps working, but the system may stop it sooner.
Asks GitHub for a new version every few hours in the background, even when the app is closed. If GitHub is blocked, the check goes through DNS-over-HTTPS and known GitHub addresses.
Could not check for updates. GitHub may be unavailable on this network.
To install the update, allow this app to install unknown apps. Android will open the setting; enable it and press Update again.
Install the update over the existing app only if it is signed with the same key. Otherwise Android will refuse and you will have to uninstall the app first — settings will be lost.
Automatic updates are on: new versions are checked, verified and installed in the background. You can change this in “Notifications and updates”.
New secret generated — save to apply
Notification permission is required to keep the proxy alive in the background
Press Start, then add the proxy in Telegram

Local MTProto proxy that bridges Telegram traffic over WebSocket to Telegram's own web endpoints, with Cloudflare and plain TCP fallbacks.

Set it up in Telegram: Settings → Data and Storage → Proxy → Add proxy → MTProto, using the host, port and secret shown on the main screen. Tapping “Open in Telegram” fills that in automatically.

The proxy only listens locally; it does not intercept other apps' traffic.

If Telegram is slow or does not connect on mobile data, open “Bypass blocking” — each option there explains what it does.

The proxy listens on %1$s:%2$d with secret:

%3$s

Start it, then tap “Open in Telegram” to add the proxy automatically.
For mobile internet that only lets \"allowed\" sites through

When an operator switches to whitelist mode, only servers on its allowed list can be reached; Telegram and Cloudflare are cut off and no setting on the phone alone gets past that. The way through is your own small relay on a server whose address is on the list (usually hosting inside the country). The relay forwards Telegram\'s already-encrypted traffic and sees nothing inside it.

Examples:
relay.example.ru
ws://203.0.113.7:8080
wss://relay.example.ru?ip=203.0.113.7&sni=vk.com&key=SECRET
ip — connect to this address, sni — the name the network sees, key — the relay password, verify=0 — accept a self-signed certificate.

Send Telegram through the relay right away and keep a ready connection for every data center. Turn on under whitelists or when the relay is simply the fastest route. Otherwise the relay joins the race with the other routes and wins only when it answers first.
How to set up a relay

By default TLS (port 443) and plain ws:// (port 80) to the Cloudflare proxy and Workers are tried side by side, and the app remembers which one works on this network: since 16.11 many ISPs drop TLS to Cloudflare specifically. Turn this on to use port 80 only (upstream \"no secure\" mode). Telegram traffic stays encrypted either way.

Check the certificates of Telegram, Cloudflare and relays against the system store, as the desktop version does since 1.10.4. Turn off only on old devices where connections fail with certificate errors in the log.

A found update is downloaded, checked (SHA-256 from GitHub, package name and signing key) and installed without a dialog on Android 12+; older Android versions show one confirmation. The proxy restarts by itself afterwards.
Tap to see what\'s new and install.
